vo: This is Hotsauce, a free, open source office suite for small teams, running on your own server. Here's a quick look at each app. The day starts on Today: your meetings, your tasks, and what changed since yesterday, on one page.
Docs are plain Markdown files, kept in Git. Link docs with two square brackets, and step back through every version to see who changed what.
Meetings takes the notes for you, and no bot joins your call. Your rough notes and the transcript become clean notes, with decisions and action items.
Ask a question across every meeting and doc, and the answer points back to its sources. Hotsauce also writes a brief, so your AI agents already know what you're working on.
Action items land in Tasks. Type one in plain words, or just ramble for a few seconds, and Hotsauce sorts it into a clean list.
Notes hold the small stuff. Color them, pin them, or turn them into checklists.
Check-ins ask the team a question on a schedule, like what will you get done this week, and gather everyone's answers in one place.
Clips replaces the meeting you didn't need. Record your screen and talk it through. Whoever watches gets a transcript and a summary.
Dictate turns talking into clean text. Hold a key on your Mac and speak into any app, or leave a voice note from your phone.

The Mac app sets itself up one step at a time. Enter your team's workspace, and sign in with Google, which connects Dictate too. Try it in the practice box, then see each permission it needs, with a plain reason for every one. Skip one, and it asks again later.
Found a bug, or have an idea? Send feedback from any page. Attach a picture of the page you were on with one click, then follow what happens to it.
And there's more: whiteboards for sketching ideas together, a people directory, shared files, forms, and Briefcast, a morning briefing you can play like a podcast.
Hotsauce is free and open source, and it deploys to Cloudflare in minutes. Get it at hotsauce dot work.
